author: Mark Magnier
description:
US President Donald Trump claimed on Wednesday that the US held a significant lead over China in artificial intelligence, touted what he termed unprecedented levels of inbound US investment and said he was thrilled about Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington later this month.
The president’s bravado comes as inflation and oil prices rise, his war of choice with Iran drags on and his polling numbers hit new lows ahead of the US midterm elections in November.
“AI is going up, and...
title: Trump calls Xi’s Washington visit ‘exciting’, but claims US leads China in AI race

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
US lawmakers targeted China and birth tourism on Wednesday for the second time this week during hearings on birthright citizenship, a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in June but still under challenge from the Trump administration..
“The demand for US citizenship for the children of Chinese nationals has led to unscrupulous companies assisting these individuals for profit,” said Chip Roy, a Republican from Texas.
Wednesday’s Judiciary hearing was called to review June’s Supreme...
title: US lawmakers target China, birth tourism as citizenship fight intensifies

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has issued its first dedicated declaration on nuclear safety and security, condemning attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities and outlining practical cooperation, amid tensions over Iran’s nuclear programme and wider questions of global nuclear governance.
The document was adopted on Tuesday at the bloc’s 25th anniversary summit in Bishkek by leaders of all 10 member states – China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan...
title: SCO takes landmark stand on nuclear security as Iran comes under renewed attack

author: Orange Wang
description:
As China and Russia rallied dozens of countries in Bishkek to shape a multipolar world order, Washington’s envoys were splitting the spotlight by meeting several Central Asian presidents in the Kyrgyz capital this week.
The manoeuvring showed that the US was likely to continue its outreach to the region and seek to blunt Beijing’s influence, but it would be “unrealistic” for Washington to force Central Asian countries to choose sides, according to a leading Chinese analyst.
US Senator Steve...
title: In Bishkek, US envoys shadow the SCO summit in challenge on Beijing and Moscow’s turf

author: Mohamed Ibrahim Hafez,Sebastian Contin Trillo-Figueroa
description:
China is beginning to match its economic presence abroad with the military reach required to operate across it.
The clearest evidence came from Egypt. Chinese J-16 fighters flew there recently, supported by YU-20 tankers that refuelled them in the air. The Chinese jets are taking part in Egypt’s “Eagles of Civilisation” alongside Egyptian Rafales and MiG-29s. This is the first time China has sent the jets to Africa, providing experience in moving a combat force across continents and operating...
title: China-Egypt joint drills a show of Beijing’s military reach

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Japan’s plans to transfer ageing warships to the Philippines and Indonesia could turn older military hardware into geopolitical leverage, deepening regional security ties while helping Tokyo counterbalance Beijing’s growing influence, observers say.
Such transfers, they said, fit into Tokyo’s broader security assistance toolkit to strengthen partners’ capabilities and forge longer-term defence relationships through equipment, training, maintenance and interoperability – expanding Japan’s...
title: How Japan aims to convert ageing warships into leverage to counter China

author: Dewey Sim
description:
As the US resumes strikes on Iran to force an end to the six-month-old war, Tehran is turning to multilateral groupings like the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and Brics for political and diplomatic cover.
At the SCO summit in Bishkek on Tuesday, world leaders made veiled references to the instability in the Middle East without naming the United States directly, in apparent tacit backing for Iran.
The Bishkek Declaration closing the summit, meanwhile, explicitly condemned the military...
title: Iran wins SCO backing against US strikes: will it be enough?

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
A delegation from the European Commission has been locked in talks with Chinese officials in Beijing, as the sides look to find a diplomatic off-ramp from a looming trade war before an October deadline set by Brussels.
The EU team was spearheaded by Denis Redonnet, the bloc’s top trade enforcement officer, who was recently made point person on China trade policy – a recognition that in EU circles, talk of partnership has largely been usurped by rivalry and competition.
Later this month, the...
title: EU trade enforcers descend on Beijing demanding China fix ‘untenable’ imbalances

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping touched down in Egypt on Tuesday, the second stop in a potentially busy month of travel that will probably conclude with a White House meeting.
“Once you drink from the Nile, you are destined to return,” the Chinese leader said on arrival at Cairo International Airport. Xi is likely to sign economic agreements with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi on Wednesday as part of his first trip in a decade to the most-populous Arab nation and his first Middle East stop...
title: Xi makes world tour ahead of White House summit

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
International students in the United States are facing new hurdles when it comes to internships and off-campus work after several major universities paused or restricted certain forms of Curricular Practical Training (CPT).
CPT is a form of work authorisation that allows foreign students to take part in internships and other practical training related to their studies.
The changes follow two August directives from the Student and Exchange Visitor Programme (SEVP), a division of US Immigration...
title: US universities curb international student internships following federal warning

author: Adriel Kasonta
description:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) was born 25 years ago as a modest mechanism for managing borders between China, Russia and four Central Asian states. At its anniversary summit in Bishkek this week, it looks more consequential – and harder for the United States to dismiss.
The timing is important. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine remains unresolved, while the war between Iran and the US has turned the Persian Gulf into another theatre of strategic competition, with energy markets again...
title: How the SCO chips away at US power without an alliance system

author: Meredith Chen
description:
A Boeing 747-8 operated by Air China reportedly suffered a fuel leak at New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport early on Monday, leading to the flight being cancelled.
No injuries were reported in or around the aircraft, which was expected to operate flight CA982 from New York to Beijing that day. The leak is said to have occurred between 1am and 2am while the plane was parked at the gate, according to posts on Chinese social media.

It was being refuelled when the fuel truck moved away...
title: Air China Boeing 747 grounded in New York following gate refuelling incident

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Chinese scientists have identified a genetic barrier that makes it hard to crossbreed African and Asian rice varieties – a discovery that could lay the foundations for creating high-yielding hybrids.
While both Asian and African cultivated rice varieties have distinct strengths, crossing them often produces offspring with sterile pollen and low yields.
A research team has now identified three genes that act as a barrier to reproduction – and also a possible way round the problem.


“This...
title: Chinese research team may have cracked secret to crossbreeding Asian and African rice

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
An American journalist who lived in Beijing, worked for Chinese state media and pleaded guilty to helping Beijing collect US intelligence was sentenced on Tuesday to two years in federal prison.
Thomas Weir Pauken II, 51, was also sentenced to three years of supervised release and barred from overseas travel during that period, according to the US Justice Department. He also used the alias Tom McGregor. His father, Thomas Pauken, chaired the Texas Republican Party in the 1990s and later ran for...
title: US journalist jailed for 2 years for working as a Chinese agent

author: William Zheng,Yuanyue Dang
description: For more, check out the South China Morning Post’s full anti-corruption data bank project:
title: China’s corruption investigation procedures

author: Ling Xin
description:
China has pulled off two-way laser communication between Earth and the moon, making it only the second nation after the United States to do so. But the data rates it achieved were well behind those recorded by Nasa more than a decade ago, and that has left space experts scratching their heads.
Using telescopes in Yunnan province and an experimental satellite that is now orbiting the moon after a launch mishap in 2024, the team recorded a downlink speed of 100 megabits per second and an uplink...
title: China’s 2026 moon laser communication speed is slower than Nasa’s in 2013

author: Tony Zhao
description:
China has spent years articulating its preferred principles for the world order. In June, it went a step further, bringing many of them together in a white paper on global governance and setting out how its Global Governance Initiative should translate principles into practice. Two ambitions sat side by side: an “equal and orderly multipolar world” and a “universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalisation”.
The timing is telling. World leaders will gather in New York this month for the...
title: China’s multipolar world order must prove it can be peaceful

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
When six Chinese heavy transport planes entered European airspace in April 2022, it was not just their cargo that drew international attention.
Bound for Serbia, the Y-20 aircraft had flown thousands of kilometres from China carrying components of the Chinese-made FK-3 surface-to-air missile system.
A second wave of six aircraft followed, bringing the operation to 12 sorties in what was then China’s biggest overseas airlift involving the strategic cargo plane.
Coming just weeks after Russia...
title: Tanker, transporter, controller: China’s Y-20 family expands its Pacific reach
